title: evaluation-form template variables
description: Values for templates/evaluation-form.md.j2 and templates/evaluation-form.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from evaluation-form.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

build_reference.title: Build reference
build_reference.description: Exactly what you evaluated - the staging URL, the build number or the prototype link with its version. "The live site" ages between writing this and someone reading it.

date.title: Date
date.description: Date of the pass, ISO. Findings are against a build that will move within days; without the date, a fixed issue reappears in the next report as a regression that never happened.

evaluator.title: Evaluator
evaluator.description: Who did this pass. Heuristic evaluation is single-evaluator by nature and each one finds a different third of the issues, so the name is what makes a second pass worth running.

focus_heuristics.title: Focus heuristics
focus_heuristics.description: Which of the ten you concentrated on and why. All ten in one pass gives each about the same attention as a glance; naming two or three is a stronger claim than pretending to cover all.

product_feature.title: Product feature
product_feature.description: The product or flow being evaluated, named as a user would find it. Evaluate one flow properly rather than a whole product thinly - the thin pass finds only what a screenshot would.

scope_screens.title: Scope screens
scope_screens.description: Which screens and flows you actually walked, and which you did not. The unwalked half is the part a reader will otherwise assume was clean, and that assumption is where the escape happens.
